## Bullfrog spa filters: short thread, long thread, and coreless cartridges

URL: https://myspafilter.com/guides/bullfrog-threaded-and-coreless-filters/
Last updated: 2026-10-27

How Unicel, Pleatco and Leisure Time describe Bullfrog 8CH-950, 8CH-951, and the coreless PBF17 and PBF40 cartridges, including the cage-and-cap note and the area ratings that do not match.

Bullfrog’s older threaded cartridges are not one part. Unicel marks 8CH-950 discontinued and says to use 8CH-951[5]. Pleatco lists PBF35 against a short-thread OEM (10-2785, 2003–2012) and PBF36 against the long-thread OEM 10-2870 (2013–2017)[2]. From 2017, Pleatco’s spec table adds coreless cartridges PBF17 (OEM 10-00281) and PBF40 (OEM 10-00282), and Leisure Time says those need the correct filter cage and cap installed[43][42].

## Two threaded 8" cartridges, and a discontinued number

Bullfrog used a top-load cartridge with a handle and an SAE thread before it moved some models to a coreless design. The threaded pair is where people order the wrong length.

PartOEM as printedSizeThreadWhat the source says

Unicel 8CH-950 / Pleatco PBF35 / Filbur FC-0536Unicel: 10-1035. Pleatco’s PBF35 spec row: 10-27858" × 6"2" SAE, described by Pleatco as the short threadUnicel: discontinued, use 8CH-951. Pleatco: Bullfrog 35, 2003–2012[5][2]

Unicel 8CH-951 / Pleatco PBF3610-28708" × 5-3/4"2" SAE, described by Pleatco as the long threadPleatco: Bullfrog 35, 2013–2017. Unicel’s note says the original element is 35 sq ft and that the spec table rates 8CH-951 at 40 sq ft[5][2]

Read the disagreements instead of averaging them. Unicel’s OEM for 8CH-950 is 10-1035. Pleatco’s spec row for the cartridge it cross-references, PBF35, prints OEM 10-2785, not 10-1035[2]. Unicel says 8CH-950 is discontinued in favor of 8CH-951. The length on our rows is 6" for 8CH-950 and 5-3/4" for 8CH-951, and Unicel also says 8CH-951 replaces a Bullfrog element with a 6" overall length and a shorter threaded end[5]. Area is not settled in a single number either: Unicel’s note says the original cartridge is 35 sq ft and that the spec table rates 8CH-951 at 40 sq ft. The compiled size field on our 8CH-951 page shows 50 sq ft. Do not buy this cartridge by the square-foot figure. Buy it by OEM 10-2870 if that is the number on a 2013–2017 long-thread filter, and compare the thread length and the 5-3/4" body with the old one.

There is also a smaller threaded Bullfrog row, 6CH-940, with no OEM number in the catalogs we used: 6" × 8-1/4", semi-circular handle, injection-molded 1-1/2" SAE thread, Pleatco PWW50P3, Filbur FC-0359, 50 sq ft on the row. No model years are attached. If your cartridge is about 6" across rather than 8", start there and measure.

## Coreless cartridges: the fabric is not the whole filter

Pleatco’s 2023 spec table lists two Bullfrog coreless cartridges for 2017 onward[2]. Neither has a Unicel number in the 2026 guide, which is why those pages are filed under the Pleatco part.

- PBF17, OEM 10-00281. Pleatco prints 6-5/8" × 6-1/4", 3-3/8" open top, 4-1/2" open bottom, and calls it the Bullfrog 18 coreless cartridge, 2017 to current. Our row shows 18 sq ft from that Pleatco description. Leisure Time rates the same OEM number at about 27 sq ft, lists Bullfrog STIL spas, and says 2015–2017 STIL spas need Filter Core Cage and Cap Assembly 10-00417. The listing also says the cartridge is coreless and that the correct filter cage and cap must be installed[43].

- PBF40, OEM 10-00282. Pleatco prints 8" × 6-1/4" with the same style of open ends and calls it the Bullfrog 30 coreless cartridge, 2017 to current (30 sq ft on our Pleatco-based row). Leisure Time rates OEM 10-00282 at 50 sq ft, says 2013–2017 A/R/X spas need the Filter Core Cage and Cap Assembly, and says 2023-and-newer A Series models use Simplicity flat filters instead[42]. The fitment we publish from that listing is A Series and R Series for 2018–2022, and X Series for 2018–2026.

The area gap (18 vs about 27, and 30 vs 50) is the same kind of catalog disagreement described in why same-size filters show different square feet. For a coreless Bullfrog filter it has an extra consequence: the pleated sock is only half the assembly. Leisure Time’s sentence is to install the correct cage and cap[43][42]. If the cage is broken, a new sock does not replace the cage. If the spa is a 2023-or-newer A Series, the same listing says the filter is a Simplicity flat filter, not PBF40. Confirm that on the listing or in the spa before you order a coreless cartridge.

## Open-end Bullfrog rows that are not the threaded 8"

Bullfrog also appears on two open-end cartridges that other brands use: C-4335 (4-15/16" × 9-1/4", 2-1/8" open both ends, 35 sq ft, Pleatco PRB35-IN) and C-4950 (4-15/16" × 13-5/16", same open ends, 50 sq ft, Pleatco PRB50-IN). Those rows do not carry a Bullfrog OEM number in our table. They are size matches from the catalogs, not a model-year list. If your Bullfrog cartridge is a short 8" threaded filter or a coreless sock, these 4-15/16" parts are the wrong family. The way to tell is the end cap, which is the subject of open-end vs threaded hot tub filters.

## What to photograph before you order

- The OEM number, especially 10-1035, 10-2785, 10-2870, 10-00281 or 10-00282.

- The overall length. A 6" threaded cartridge and a 5-3/4" threaded cartridge are both “about six inches” if you only glance at them.

- The thread: short versus long is the distinction Pleatco prints for the 2003–2012 and 2013–2017 Bullfrog 35 cartridges[2].

- Whether there is a plastic cage around the media. Coreless cartridges are open fabric over a cage. Threaded cartridges have a handle and a screw bottom.

- The series badge (STIL, A, R, X) and the year, then check Bullfrog filters by series and year.

Unicel’s maintenance page still applies after you have the right part: cartridges are replaced when cleaning stops restoring flow, not on a calendar alone, and acid washing is the step Unicel warns against doing casually[4][6]. Installation steps that every brand shares — power off, don’t run the spa empty of a filter — are in how to install a hot tub filter.

## Intex PureSpa and Bestway Lay-Z-Spa filters: S1, S2 and Type VI

URL: https://myspafilter.com/guides/intex-and-bestway-inflatable-spa-filters/
Last updated: 2026-10-27

Which inflatable hot tub uses the Intex Type S1 cartridge, which uses Type S2, and which Bestway tubs use the Type VI cartridge. Sizes and part numbers from the manufacturers’ pages.

Intex PureSpa tubs use two different cartridges. Type S1 is sold as 29001E (two-pack), 29011E (six-pack) and single part 11692; Unicel lists it as C-4317 and Pleatco as PIN4PAIR, at 4-1/4" × 2-15/16"[32][33][5][2]. Type S2 is 29012E (two-pack) and single part 13435, and Intex gives the size as 3.375" × 5.125" for PureSpa models whose cartridge is built into the control unit[34][35]. Bestway’s SaluSpa Type VI cartridge is 4.2" × 3.1", and Lay-Z-Spa says Type VI fits every Lay-Z-Spa except the Monte Carlo[36][37].

## Why the set number matters more than the brand name

An inflatable spa does not use the 6" or 8" cartridge a hardshell Hot Spring or Caldera uses. The cartridges are a few inches each way, and Intex has sold two of them under names that look alike. The set number on the box or on the spa, including the letters at the end, is what Intex’s own compatible-item lists use. A retailer search for “Intex spa filter” mixes S1 and S2. The lists do not.

These cartridges are also absent from the usual hardshell cross-reference in one important way. S1 is in the Unicel 2026 guide and the Pleatco 2023 catalog. S2 and the Bestway Type VI cartridge are not in those catalogs, so there is no Unicel C-number or Pleatco P-number to fall back on. You order the manufacturer’s part, then compare the size Intex or Bestway prints.

## Type S1: 29001E, 29011E and part 11692

Intex’s product page for the Type S1 twin pack is SKU 29001E, described as the PureSpa replacement filter. The six-pack is SKU 29011E. The replacement-part page for a single cartridge is part 11692, and that page is the compatible-item list[32][33]. Unicel prints OEM 29001 and 11692 and lists the cartridge as C-4317. Pleatco’s spec table prints OEM 29001E as PIN4PAIR, which is a two-cartridge pack, not a different body[5][2].

What you might seeWhat it refers to

29001EIntex Type S1 twin pack

29011EIntex Type S1 six-pack

11692Intex single S1 replacement cartridge

Unicel C-4317Unicel’s listing of that S1 body

Pleatco PIN4PAIRPleatco’s two-cartridge pack for OEM 29001E

Body size is the number the catalogs agree on: 4-1/4" diameter by 2-15/16" long, rated 4 sq ft on the Unicel row. The end-cap opening is the number they do not agree on. Unicel prints 2-1/16" open at both ends. Pleatco prints 1-5/8"[5][2]. Our C-4317 page keeps both and treats the body size as the match. Hold a new cartridge against the old one if you are crossing from one brand’s listing to the other.

Intex’s 11692 compatible-item list is the model list on that page. It includes, among others, PureSpa set numbers 28403E, 28405E, 28407E and 28409E (Intex marks those four 2019 sets with the year), plus 28421E, 28425E, 28427E, 28429E, 28431E, 28433EP, 28433WL, 28435E, 28439E, 28441E and 28453E[33]. A retailer listing for 29001E has named extra set numbers that are not on Intex’s list. We do not add those. If your set number is not on the 11692 page, do not assume S1 fits. Check the S2 list next, because several of the same digits move to S2 when the suffix changes.

## Type S2: the suffix is the whole story

Intex’s S2 twin pack is SKU 29012E. The single replacement is part 13435. Intex prints the size as 3.375" × 5.125" and says the S2 is only for PureSpa models with the cartridge built into the control unit[34]. That is a different shape from S1: S1 is a short, wide cartridge (4-1/4" across and under 3" tall). S2 is narrower and taller. They do not swap.

The 13435 compatible-item list names 28425EG, 28425EH, 28427EG, 28427EH, 28439EH, 28441EH and 28449EH[35]. Compare that with the S1 list. 28425E, 28427E, 28439E and 28441E are on the S1 list. The same digits with an EG or EH suffix are on the S2 list. “28425” without the suffix is not a filter choice. Read the full set number on the box or in the manual.

Our 29012E page also records that one retailer listing prints 3.5" × 6.25" per filter. That figure does not match Intex’s 3.375" × 5.125", so the page shows Intex’s size. There is no Unicel or Pleatco equivalent in the catalogs we use. Search by 29012E or 13435, not by a C-number.

## Bestway Type VI, and the Monte Carlo exception

Bestway’s US product page for the SaluSpa Type VI two-pack gives the size as 4.2" across and 3.1" tall, for Bestway’s SaluSpa line[36]. The Lay-Z-Spa UK page for Filter Cartridge VI says it is compatible with all Lay-Z-Spa hot tubs except the Monte Carlo, which has its own rigid-spa cartridge[37]. Neither of those manufacturer pages is where we got a numeric part. The retail model 58323 / 58323E-BW is the number recorded on our Bestway 58323 page from the retailer listing that page cites. Order from a listing whose title says Type VI, and compare 4.2" × 3.1" with the old cartridge. If the spa is a Monte Carlo, stop and use the rigid-spa cartridge Lay-Z-Spa sells for that model. The Type VI page says it does not fit.

Unicel, Pleatco and Filbur do not list a Type VI equivalent. There is no honest C-number to print, and the page does not invent one.

## How these small cartridges get used

S1 and S2 are small media areas next to a hardshell cartridge of 30 to 75 sq ft. Intex sells them in multi-packs because owners go through them, not because the spa holds two different types at once. A twin pack is two of the same cartridge in the box. It is not a statement that the spa takes an S1 and an S2 together.

Nothing on Intex’s S1 or S2 pages reprints the hose-and-soak procedure Unicel publishes for pleated spa cartridges[4]. Follow the care card that came with the spa. What does transfer from the hardshell manuals is the reason to keep a spare: Jacuzzi says not to run a spa with no filter installed, because unfiltered water carries debris to the pump and the heater[10]. That warning is not written for PureSpa specifically. It is the reason a two-pack is useful. Rinse or swap before the little cartridge collapses, and see what a clogged or missing filter does for the flow faults hardshell controls display when a cartridge plugs.

If you also own a hardshell tub, do not borrow its cartridge. A Hot Spring C-6430 is 6" × 10-1/2". It will not fit a PureSpa. The size lookup will show you that immediately if you type the diameter and length.

## A short decision list

- Find the full set number, letters included.

- If it is on Intex’s 11692 list, you need Type S1 (29001E, 29011E or 11692). Open the S1 page.

- If it is on Intex’s 13435 list, or the letters are EG or EH on a number that looks like an S1 set, you need Type S2 (29012E or 13435). Open the S2 page.

- If the spa is a SaluSpa or a Lay-Z-Spa other than Monte Carlo, you need Type VI, about 4.2" × 3.1". Open the Type VI page.

- If it is a Monte Carlo, use Lay-Z-Spa’s rigid-spa cartridge, not Type VI[37].

Hardshell cross-reference, for when the tub is not inflatable, starts at how Filbur, Unicel and Pleatco numbers compare.

## Sundance and Jacuzzi look-alike filters: core plugs, bottom holes and handles

URL: https://myspafilter.com/guides/sundance-and-jacuzzi-look-alike-filters/
Last updated: 2026-10-27

Cartridges that share a Sundance or Jacuzzi OEM number, or a diameter and length, and still differ: C-8326 vs C-8327, C-7465 vs C-7466, 6CH-960 vs 6CH-961, and OEM 373045.

Several Sundance and Jacuzzi cartridges share a body and not a detail Unicel bothers to print. C-8326 and C-8327 are both 8-7/16" × 19", 125 sq ft, OEM 6540-488; Unicel says C-8326 has a core plug and fits spas before 2006, and C-8327 has no core plug and fits spas after 2005[5]. C-7465 and C-7466 are both 7-1/2" × 14-3/4" castle-top cartridges at 65 sq ft; the bottom opening is 2-1/16" (OEM 6540-480) or 2-5/8" (OEM 6540-481)[5]. Match the OEM number, then the note in the spec table.

## The 125 sq ft pair: core plug or no core plug

C-8326 and C-8327 are the cartridges people shorten to “the big Sundance filter.” The spec rows print the same outside size and the same ends: 8-7/16" diameter, 19" long, a 1-1/2" male slip fitting on top, and a 2-1/2" open bottom with a beveled edge. Both are rated 125 sq ft. Both are tied to OEM 6540-488. Pleatco lists PSD125-2000 and Filbur lists FC-2780 against that OEM number[5][2][31].

Unicel still splits them. The note on C-8326 says it contains a core block or plug, and the fitment Unicel gives is Sundance spas before 2006. The note on C-8327 says there is no core block or plug, the fitment is Sundance spas after 2005, and Unicel also prints OEM 6540-507 on that row. A Leisure Time listing describes C-8326 and C-8327 as the same cartridge[44]. Unicel does not. When a dealer treats them as one part and the manufacturer’s filter guide treats the plug as the difference, keep the plug. Look down the core of the old cartridge. If your spa is dated before 2006 and the cartridge you removed has the plug, C-8326 is the row Unicel points at. If it is after 2005 and there is no plug, C-8327 is the row. If you cannot see a plug and cannot date the spa, order by the full OEM number on the cap (6540-488 or 6540-507) and compare the new cartridge with the old one before you install it.

## The 65 sq ft castle-top pair: the bottom hole changes

C-7465 and C-7466 are both 7-1/2" × 14-3/4", both have a castle top, and both are rated 65 sq ft. The bottom inside diameter is the spec line that changes.

UnicelOEMBottomPleatcoFilbur

C-74656540-4802-1/16" openPSD65FC-2730

C-74666540-4812-5/8" openPSD65-2FC-2740

Pleatco’s “-2” on PSD65-2 is doing the same job as the different OEM number: it marks the larger bottom opening. Filbur splits them into FC-2730 and FC-2740[31]. A castle top tells you that you are in this family. It does not tell you which bottom you have. Measure the open end, or read 6540-480 versus 6540-481. The fitting guide open-end vs threaded filters shows the same pattern on other brands.

## Same OEM numbers, different top: 6CH-960 and 6CH-961

Jacuzzi 6CH-960 and 6CH-961 are both 6-3/4" × 15-1/2" cartridges with a 2" SAE thread, and Unicel prints the same OEM set on both rows: 6540-164, 6540-476 and 6541-383. The area on the rows is 75 sq ft, with a note that square footage is 75 or 60 depending on the OEM part number[5]. The tops differ. 6CH-960 is printed with a semi-circular handle. 6CH-961 is printed “open with slots,” and Unicel says it requires an injection-molded semi-circular handle that is not furnished. Pleatco splits them into PJW60TL-F2S and PJW60TL-OT-F2S. Filbur lists FC-2800 and FC-2715. If your old cartridge has the handle molded on, you are looking at the 6CH-960 description. If the top is open and the handle is a separate piece, you are looking at the 6CH-961 description. Ordering the one that does not include the handle, when yours is molded on, gives you a cap you did not have before.

## One Jacuzzi OEM number printed on two areas

Jacuzzi OEM 373045 appears on two open-end cartridges of the same body size and different media area: C-4326 at 25 sq ft and C-4950 at 50 sq ft. Both are 4-15/16" × 13-5/16" with 2-1/8" open ends. The note on the C-4950 row says the same OEM part number is listed for 25 and 50 sq ft[5]. This is the upgrade pattern Unicel describes elsewhere: more pleats in the same can, which is the subject of why same-size filters have different square-foot ratings. Pleatco lists PRB25-IN and PRB50-IN for that size family. If the only number you have is 373045, you still have to know whether the cartridge you removed is the 25 sq ft or the 50 sq ft version. Count the pleats if the printing is gone. Unicel’s own lookup instructions include a pleat count within about two pleats[5].

## J-460 and the shared 6540-series numbers

Sundance and Jacuzzi Premium share a large family of 6540-series OEM numbers. Sundance 5CH-402 and Jacuzzi 5CH-402 are both OEM 6540-723: 5-3/16" × 10-3/4", bar handle, 2" male MPT, 50 sq ft. Sharing the number across the two brands means the cartridge is the same row, not that every Jacuzzi takes every Sundance cartridge.

The opposite warning is on the J-460. Leisure Time’s listing for 6CH-945 (OEM 6540-498, 6" × 13-1/2", 2" SAE, 45 sq ft, Pleatco PJP45-F2S) says J-460 spas used several cartridges that are not interchangeable, and that you should confirm size and thread against the old filter[45]. A J-460 owner who orders “the J-460 filter” from a single photo has not finished the job. Measure length and look at the thread. The Jacuzzi model-year lookup and the Sundance lookup are the indexes. All Jacuzzi cartridges and all Sundance cartridges are the full tables.

## What to write down

- The full OEM number, including 6540-488 versus 6540-507, 6540-480 versus 6540-481, and 6540-164 versus the other numbers on that cap.

- Whether you can see a core plug.

- The bottom opening or the thread, measured, not guessed from the length.

- Whether the handle is molded on or is a separate piece.

- The year of the spa when the Unicel note is “before 2006” or “after 2005.”

Installation after you have the match is covered in how to install a hot tub filter. If the spa throws a flow code the first time the new cartridge runs, the code list is in flow errors and the filter.

## Master Spas Eco-Pur filters: outer cartridges, the inner element, and the stand pipe

URL: https://myspafilter.com/guides/master-spas-eco-pur-filters/
Last updated: 2026-10-27

Unicel’s dates and installation notes for Master Spas Eco-Pur cartridges: C-7330 (2002–2005), C-8341 (2006 on, two required), the C-3310AM inner element, and when to remove the black stand pipe.

Unicel splits Master Spas Eco-Pur filtration into two eras. C-7330 is the outer cartridge for 2002–2005 (7" × 7-1/4", 30 sq ft). C-8341 is the outer cartridge from 2006 on (8" × 6-3/4", 40 sq ft), and Unicel says two of those 40 sq ft cartridges are required[5]. The small C-3310AM element (3-7/8" × 7", antimicrobial media) is used with either outer cartridge. On the threaded Eco-Pur replacements, Unicel says to remove the black stand pipe[5].

## Eco-Pur is an assembly, not a single cartridge

Master Spas cartridges fall into two groups in the Unicel 2026 guide: ordinary threaded top-load cartridges, and the Eco-Pur system, which pairs an outer cartridge with a small inner element. Ordering “a Master Spas filter” does not say which half you need, or whether the spa holds one outer cartridge or two. The notes below are Unicel’s, from the Master Spas section of the 2026 guide and the spec table[5].

UnicelRole Unicel gives itSizeEndsPleatco / Filbur

C-7330Eco-Pur outer, 2002–20057" × 7-1/4", 30 sq ft4-1/8" open both endsPMA30-2002-R / FC-1003

C-8341Eco-Pur outer, 2006 to present; two 40 sq ft cartridges required8" × 6-3/4", 40 sq ft4" open with a raised ring, both endsPMA45-2004-R / FC-1007

C-3310AMAntimicrobial inner element, used with C-7330 or C-83413-7/8" × 7", 8 sq ft2-3/16" open both endsPMA10; no Filbur number on our row

Count what comes out of the housing. If you remove two large cartridges and one slim element, that is the C-8341 arrangement Unicel describes, and you replace both outers plus the inner on its own schedule. If you remove one outer and one inner from a 2002–2005 system, C-7330 is the outer Unicel names. The diameters differ (7" versus 8"), so a 2002 outer does not take the place of a 2006 outer. Pleatco’s numbers carry the year in the part itself: PMA30-2002-R and PMA45-2004-R[2]. Filbur lists FC-1003 and FC-1007[31].

C-3310AM is not a substitute for the outer. It is 3-7/8" across. Unicel calls out antimicrobial media and says it is used with a C-7330 or a C-8341[5]. Replacing only the inner leaves the outer media in place. Replacing only the outer leaves the inner element in place. They are different part numbers because they are different pieces.

## The stand-pipe note on the threaded replacements

Other Master Spas rows are threaded cartridges rather than the open-end Eco-Pur outers, and Unicel attaches an installation note to them.

- 6CH-352, OEM PMA-R1. 6" × 8", semi-circular handle, 2" male MPT, 35 sq ft, Pleatco PAS40-F2M. Unicel says to remove the black stand pipe. Filbur cross-references 6CH-352 to FC-0312 but lists FC-0312 at 6" × 7", not 6" × 8"[5][31]. When the two catalogs disagree on length, measure the cartridge you removed. Do not average 7" and 8" into a length neither book printed.

- 7CH-322. 7" × 8", semi-circular handle, 2" male MPT, 32 sq ft on our row, Pleatco PAS35-F2M, Filbur FC-0420. Unicel says it is a replacement for 7" or 8" OD Eco-Pur systems, and to remove the black stand pipe for an 8" OD system[5].

- 4CH-935 and 4CH-949 are Unicel’s replacements for 5" OD Eco-Pur systems. 4CH-935 is 4-15/16" × 9-1/4". 4CH-949 is 4-15/16" × 13-1/2". Neither row has an OEM number in our table, and Unicel says to verify the overall length. “Verify OAL” means measure. A 9-1/4" cartridge and a 13-1/2" cartridge are both 4-15/16" in diameter and they are not the same part.

The stand pipe is a plastic tube in the filter well. Unicel’s instruction is to remove it when you install these replacements. That instruction is on the cartridge, not a general rule for every Master Spas model. If your housing does not have a black stand pipe, there is nothing to remove. If it does, and you are installing 6CH-352 or an 8" application of 7CH-322, the note says it comes out[5]. Forcing a threaded cartridge down over a stand pipe the note says to remove is how a new filter fails to seat.

## How this differs from “buy a spare”

A second set of cartridges, which Unicel, Pleatco and Jacuzzi recommend so one set can soak while the other is in the spa, is a spare[4][1][10]. Two C-8341 cartridges in the housing at the same time are not a spare. They are the system Unicel says the 2006-and-later Eco-Pur filter uses. Buy two outers because the housing holds two, and keep a further spare only if you want one soaking. The guide to that distinction, including Hot Spring’s three-cartridge wells, is spas that use more than one filter.

## What to check before you order

- Count the large cartridges and look for a slim inner element.

- Measure the outer diameter: about 7" points at C-7330, about 8" at C-8341, about 6" at 6CH-352, about 4-15/16" at the 4CH Eco-Pur replacements.

- Read any OEM number, especially PMA-R1.

- If the spa is around 2005 or 2006, use the year Unicel prints rather than a photo of “an Eco-Pur filter.”

- Read the stand-pipe note on the page for the part you are about to buy.

- Use the Master Spas filter by series and year lookup, then the Master Spas brand table for the rows that have no year.

Threaded versus open ends are covered in open-end vs threaded hot tub filters. Length disagreements between catalogs are the same problem as the square-foot disagreements in why same-size filters differ: the outside dimensions in the two books are not always identical, so the cartridge in your hand is the measurement that counts.

## How to install a hot tub filter cartridge

URL: https://myspafilter.com/guides/how-to-install-a-hot-tub-filter/
Last updated: 2026-10-27

The install steps that Hot Spring, Jacuzzi, Sundance and Unicel actually print: power off, match the ends, do not overtighten, do not run the spa with the cartridge out, and keep a second set.

Turn the spa off, put the new cartridge in the same orientation as the one you removed, and do not overtighten the retainer. Hot Spring’s manual says to cut power before you remove filters, not to use the spa with the cartridge removed, and not to overtighten the filter retainer[9]. Jacuzzi says the same about power and about running with no filter, because debris then goes to the pump and heater, and it says to keep a second cartridge so the spa is never filter-less while one soaks[10].

## Before you open the well

Installation starts with the right part, not with the lid. If you are not sure the new cartridge matches, stop and use the part-number search or the size guide. A cartridge that is close in length and wrong on the bottom will sit in the housing and not seal. Which ends the catalogs care about is covered in open-end vs threaded hot tub filters.

Then make the spa safe to open. Hot Spring’s Hot Spot collection manual and Jacuzzi’s filter instructions both say to turn the power off before you remove the filter[9][10]. Jacuzzi’s reason is specific: it stops the pump from starting while your hands are in the well, and it avoids pulling air into the plumbing. Sundance’s air-lock procedure has you take the filter out only with the power off, purge the air, and put the filter back before you restore power[12].

## The steps the manuals share

- Power off at the spa’s disconnect or the breaker the manual names, not only by setting the jets to zero[9][10].

- Lift the old cartridge the way that spa is built. Handle-top cartridges lift by the handle. Open-end cartridges slide off a standpipe. Unicel’s general instruction is to remove the cartridge following the spa maker’s instructions[4].

- Look at which end was up. The spec table’s “top” is the end that faced you: a handle, an open hole of a stated size, or a closed cap. Put the new cartridge back the same way. On a threaded bottom, the thread goes onto the fitting you just unscrewed the old one from. On a male-slip bottom, the stub goes into the receiver. Do not flip an open-end cartridge end for end if the two holes are different sizes. Sundance C-8326, for example, has a 1-1/2" male slip on one end and a 2-1/2" opening on the other[5].

- Seat it and snug the retainer. Hot Spring says not to overtighten the filter retainer[9]. Cracking an end cap by cranking the retainer is a failed install, not a tighter seal.

- Restore power only after the cartridge is in. Sundance’s purge steps end with the filter reinstalled before power returns[12]. Hot Spring says not to use the spa with the cartridge removed[9]. Jacuzzi advises against running with no filter installed[10].

- Watch the first cycle. A flow error right after a filter change is often air or water level, not a bad new cartridge. The code-by-code version is hot tub flow errors and your filter.

## If the housing holds more than one

Some spas do not hold a single cartridge. The Leisure Time listing for Hot Spring OEM 71825 says many of those models take three of the 6" cartridges[38]. Unicel says Master Spas Eco-Pur systems from 2006 on require two C-8341 cartridges, plus the separate inner element[5]. Sundance’s 680 and 780 manuals describe a pleated outer filter and a disposable MicroClean insert, and they give those two pieces different replacement intervals[11][12]. Count the pieces you removed. Install the same count. A guide to those systems is spas that use more than one filter.

The insert is not cleaned like the outer cartridge. Sundance says never to use filter cleaners on the inner inserts, and its 680 manual specifies a low-pressure rinse and no chemicals on the insert, while the outer pleated filter is the one that gets a stronger hose rinse[11]. Putting the insert through the degreaser soak Unicel describes for a pleated cartridge is the wrong procedure for that piece.

## The second cartridge is a spare, not a stack

Unicel, Pleatco and Jacuzzi all tell owners to alternate two sets so one can be cleaned and dried while the other is in the spa[4][1][10]. Jacuzzi says a filter can go back in damp, and that letting a set dry completely is what extends its life. That second set lives on a shelf. It is not a second cartridge shoved into a housing designed for one, unless the spa’s own list says the housing holds two or three. Buying a two-pack of an Intex S1 cartridge is the same idea: the pack is spares of one type, and Intex’s lists still require you to pick S1 or S2. See Intex and Bestway filters.

## What not to do in the same visit

- Do not run the pump “just to test” with the well empty. That is the thing Jacuzzi and Hot Spring say not to do[10][9].

- Do not acid-wash a new cartridge. Acid is Unicel’s last step for mineral scale on a cartridge you are trying to save, and only after a degrease. Unicel calls acid washing a leading cause of early cartridge failure[4]. A new cartridge does not need it. The full caution is in should you acid wash a spa filter?

- Do not put any cartridge in a dishwasher. Jacuzzi says dishwashers and washing machines can warp end caps and do not clean between the pleats[10].

- Do not ignore a retainer that will not close. If the lid or the retainer will not seat, the cartridge is too long, the handle is on the wrong end, or a stand pipe Unicel told you to remove is still in the well. Master Spas notes that stand pipe on specific part numbers[5]. See Master Spas Eco-Pur filters.

## After it is in

Rinse residue matters on a cartridge you just cleaned, more than on one fresh from the package. Jacuzzi warns that cleaner left in the media foams once the jets run[10]. If you installed a cartridge that has been soaking, rinse it until the water runs clear, using the top-down hose method Unicel and Pleatco describe[4][1]. Then balance the water. A new filter does not set pH. Hot Spring’s published ranges for its own spas are a separate job, covered in how to balance pH and alkalinity.

Replace, rather than reinstall, when the media is torn, the core is collapsed, or cleaning no longer restores flow[6][1]. Those signs are listed in signs your hot tub filter is bad. Intervals by brand are in how often to replace a hot tub filter.

- Jacuzzi — Hot Tub Filter Cleaning Made Easy: https://www.jacuzzi.com/en-us/Hot-Tub-Filter-Cleaning-Made-Easy.html

## What a clogged or missing hot tub filter does

URL: https://myspafilter.com/guides/clogged-or-missing-hot-tub-filter/
Last updated: 2026-10-27

Why Hot Spring, Jacuzzi, Sundance, Gecko and the CDC treat a dirty cartridge as a flow and water-quality problem, and why the manuals say not to run the spa with the filter removed.

A clogged cartridge restricts flow. Hot Spring says that can weaken the jets, limit circulation, and trip the high-limit thermostat so the spa shuts off[9]. Jacuzzi lists cloudy water, a musty odor, and FLO or low-flow errors, and says not to run the spa with no filter installed because unfiltered water carries debris into the pump and heater[10]. The CDC’s hot-tub Legionella guidance includes replacing cartridges on the manufacturer’s schedule as part of controlling germs[14].

## A filter is a restriction on purpose, until it is too much

Pleated media works by catching oils, lotions, scale and fine particles. Unicel’s point is that the cartridge does not have a moving part that fails on a date. It plugs[6]. Some of that loading is the filter doing its job. Unicel also says cleaning too often can lower efficiency, because the cartridge uses the debris it has caught, and cleaning too rarely shortens the cartridge’s life[4]. The failure is the point where flow no longer recovers after a proper clean, or the media itself is torn or the core has collapsed[6][1].

You can see the early stage before a code appears. Jets feel weaker. The spa is louder or the water looks dull. Jacuzzi names cloudy water and a musty odor that survive a normal clean, limp pleats that do not spring back, cracked end caps, and a flow error that returns immediately after cleaning[10]. Hot Spring names discolored or worn media as a reason to replace, with the caution that color alone is not the whole test: Pleatco says white does not mean clean, and that media can discolor with age[8][3]. The checklist is in signs your hot tub filter is bad.

## What the control systems do when flow drops

Heaters in these spas are not supposed to fire when water is not moving. The panel messages are the control system saying it cannot see that flow. They are not a filter brand.

- Hot Spring’s Hot Spot manual says a clogged filter can reduce jet performance, limit flow, and trip the high-limit thermostat[9]. The 2023 Highlife manual’s E2 message is literally “NO FLOW-CHECK FILTER,” with the heater off, and it tells the owner to check and clean the filter and to call for service if the heater trips often[29].

- Sundance’s 2024 780 manual lists an excessively dirty filter as one cause of FL--1 (flow switch open), along with a bad switch or an air lock. FL--3 tells you to clean the filters and correct the water level before you call the dealer[12].

- Gecko’s troubleshooting guide for its Y-series and in.xe systems says FLO means no flow was detected while the main pump runs, and its HL (high-limit) note tells you to make sure nothing is blocking flow, including a dirty filter or a closed valve[26].

- Balboa’s TP600/TP400 guide uses HFL for reduced heater flow and LF when flow stays too low for the heater. Its checks start with low water, closed valves and too many closed jets, which sit alongside a blocked filter as reasons water is not moving[27].

The code-by-code order of checks is already written up in hot tub flow errors and your filter. The short version: power off, confirm the water level, clean or replace the cartridge, purge air, open valves, then reset the way that control describes. If the error survives a clean cartridge and a full water level, Jacuzzi and Sundance say to call a dealer[10][12].

## Taking the filter out is not a test

It is tempting to pull the cartridge, turn the jets on, and see if the error goes away. That tells you the cartridge was a restriction. It also runs the spa with no filtration, which is the state the manuals reject.

- Jacuzzi advises against running with no filter installed. Unfiltered water carries contaminants to the pumps and the heater. Jacuzzi’s alternative is a second, clean cartridge you can swap in[10].

- Hot Spring says not to use the spa with the cartridge removed[9].

- Sundance’s air-lock fix has the filter out only while you purge, and back in before power is on[12].

If you need the spa tonight and the cartridge is soaking, the second set is the supported method. Unicel and Pleatco describe the same rotation: one set in the spa, one set drying after a soak of at least an hour[4][1]. How to put the spare in without forcing the retainer is how to install a hot tub filter.

## Water quality is the other half of a missing filter

Flow codes are the mechanical symptom. The CDC’s hot-tub module on Legionella treats filtration as part of germ control, and it tells operators to replace cartridges according to the manufacturer[14]. The CDC’s hot-tub rash page tells bathers and operators to keep disinfectant and pH in range, which a filter does not do by itself[13]. A torn cartridge and a sanitizer at zero are two different failures. Test the water. Hot Spring’s published owner ranges are free chlorine 1–5 ppm, pH 7.2–7.8, total alkalinity 40–120 ppm and calcium hardness 75–150 ppm on a standard system[18]. CDC’s rash page uses a free-chlorine floor of at least 3 ppm for hot tubs and a bromine range of 4–8 ppm, and its pH band on that page is 7.0–7.8, which is not identical to Hot Spring’s 7.2–7.8[13]. Follow the manual for your spa when the numbers differ. The order of balancing is in how to balance pH and alkalinity, and sanitizer choices are in bromine, chlorine and mineral systems.

Cloudy water has a filter chapter and a chemistry chapter. Jacuzzi lists it as a filter symptom when it persists after the water is balanced[10]. If the water is cloudy and the test strip says the sanitizer is at zero, fix the sanitizer. If the sanitizer is in range and the pleats are crushed, replace the cartridge. Doing only one of those leaves the other problem in the tub.

## How a cartridge gets to that state

Heavy bather loads, oils and unbalanced water are the loads Pleatco and Unicel name[1][4]. Hot Spring notes that more use means more frequent cleaning[8]. Jacuzzi’s baseline for a family tub is a weekly rinse and a deep clean every 4–6 weeks, sooner with heavy use[10]. Cleaning technique matters as much as the calendar. A pressure washer or a stiff brush can tear the media Pleatco says not to scrub, and a torn cartridge bypasses in the sense that water takes the hole instead of the pleat[1][10]. Acid washing before the oils are removed is the failure Unicel flags as causing a permanent restriction[4]. The procedures, including what not to soak in, are in how to clean a hot tub filter and filter cleaner vs DIY soaks.

Replacement intervals are not one number. Jacuzzi says 12–24 months for pleated cartridges. Hot Spring says 2–3 years for a standard polyester cartridge and 4–6 years for TRI-X, while its maintenance page says three years[10][8][7]. Disposable inserts are on a much shorter clock: Sundance’s 780 manual says every 3 months for the small MicroClean cartridge, and the 680 manual says every 4 months for the Mini insert[12][11]. When the interval has passed and the flow codes have started, cleaning is the experiment and replacement is the result if flow does not return. Search the part from the homepage.

## How Filbur, Unicel and Pleatco numbers compare on the same spa filter

URL: https://myspafilter.com/guides/how-filbur-unicel-and-pleatco-numbers-compare/
Last updated: 2026-10-27

What an OEM number, a Unicel C-number or CH-number, a Pleatco P-number and a Filbur FC-number each refer to, with rows where the three catalogs agree and rows where they do not.

They are four names for a match, not four shapes. The spa maker’s OEM number is the one molded for that brand. Unicel prints a C-number or a CH-number. Pleatco prints a P-number and a cross-reference to the Unicel number. Filbur prints an FC-number in its own catalog[5][2][31]. When the size and the ends agree, the numbers are equivalents. When a catalog prints a different length or a different area, the page on this site says so instead of hiding the conflict.

## Four columns, one cartridge

Retail sites often list a single part number and a photo. The catalogs list the same physical cartridge once for each company that sells it. Our cartridge pages put those numbers in one place so you can search whichever one is still readable. The columns are:

- OEM. The spa maker’s number. Hot Spring 31489, Caldera 74148, Sundance 6540-488, Softub 90-802, Bullfrog 10-2870. Some cartridges accumulated several OEM numbers over the years. C-6430’s row prints 31489, 71825 and 71826[5].

- Unicel. Usually C- followed by four digits (C-6430, C-4950) or a size-series CH number (4CH-35, 6CH-940, 8CH-951). The 2026 Replacement Guide is both a cross-reference, by spa brand, and a spec table of diameter, length, ends, pleats and area[5].

- Pleatco. A P-number such as PWK30-4, PRB35-IN, PCD50N or PSD125-2000. The 2023 catalog includes a Unicel-to-Pleatco cross-reference and its own spec tables[2].

- Filbur. An FC-number such as FC-3915 or FC-2780, in the Filbur Catalog and Reference Guide, which also sorts parts by spa manufacturer[31].

A worked example that agrees: Hot Spring OEM 31489 / 71825 / 71826, Unicel C-6430, Pleatco PWK30-4, Filbur FC-3915. All three catalogs are cited on the C-6430 page for a 6" × 10-1/2" cartridge open 1-15/16" at both ends, 30 sq ft. Another that agrees: Caldera OEM 74148, Unicel C-4335, Pleatco PRB35-IN, a 4-15/16" × 9-1/4" cartridge with 2-1/8" open ends. Searching any one of those strings from the homepage should land on the same family of pages. OEM vs Unicel vs Pleatco is the shorter version of this idea. This page adds Filbur and the rows where the books diverge.

## Where the catalogs agree on size and disagree on a detail

Agreement on the body is not agreement on every cell.

- Softub 90-802. Unicel 6CH-25, Pleatco PTL20W-SV-P4 and Filbur FC-0305 all print 6" × 5-1/2" with a handle and a 1-1/2" MPT bottom. Unicel and Filbur rate it at 25 sq ft. Pleatco rates the same OEM number at 20 sq ft[5][2][31]. The Softub page keeps the disagreement visible. Size, OEM number and fitting are the match. Area is not a single number.

- Intex S1. Unicel C-4317 and Pleatco PIN4PAIR agree on 4-1/4" × 2-15/16". They do not agree on the end opening (2-1/16" versus 1-5/8")[5][2]. Details are in Intex and Bestway filters.

- Master Spas 6CH-352. Unicel prints 6" × 8". Filbur’s cross-reference to FC-0312 prints 6" × 7"[5][31]. Measure. The Eco-Pur context is in Master Spas Eco-Pur filters.

- Hot Spring 78161 / 1642301-1. Unicel offers C-6350 at 50 sq ft and C-6355 at 75 sq ft, both 6" × 14". Pleatco lists PWK35B at 35 sq ft and 6-3/8" × 14". A dealer page lists 50 sq ft and a slightly different OD again[5][2][24]. We do not collapse those into one rating. See Hot Spring sizes by collection.

Unicel’s area formula — pleat count times two, times pleat height, times usable length, divided by 144 — is why two honest measurements of “the same” cartridge can still print different square footage when the pleat count differs[5]. Why same-size filters differ walks through the groups in the spec table, including Unicel’s own upgrade notes such as C-4637 for a 25 sq ft cartridge of the same outside size.

## When a column is blank on purpose

A blank is not a zero. It means that catalog did not give us a number we are willing to print.

- C-6350 has no Pleatco equivalent on the page, because PWK35B’s printed size and area do not match that Unicel row.

- Intex 29012E and Bestway Type VI have no Unicel, Pleatco or Filbur numbers. They are not in those books. The manufacturer pages identify them.

- Bullfrog PBF17 and PBF40 are Pleatco coreless parts with no Unicel number in the 2026 guide. Inventing a C-number would make the search box lie.

- Some rows are marked unverified and kept out of the search index when we have only one source or the sources conflict on the OEM number. The dataset still lists them, with the citation, so you can see the gap. The methodology is the rule we use.

## What the spa maker says about “equivalent”

A cross-reference is the filter maker’s statement that its cartridge matches the OEM part’s size and fittings. It is not the spa maker’s statement that the aftermarket part is the one they want in the spa. Hot Spring’s maintenance page says to replace with genuine Watkins filters[7]. Jacuzzi recommends filters designed for the specific model[10]. Check the warranty before you switch. We are not Watkins, Jacuzzi, Unicel, Pleatco or Filbur, and the pages do not say an aftermarket cartridge is “genuine.” They say which numbers the catalogs tie together.

Filbur’s catalog is doing the same kind of work as the other two. On Marquis cartridges it lists the brand as Pacific Marquis, which is why a search for a Marquis OEM number can land on an FC-number you have not seen on the spa. The Marquis rows on this site cite that naming. If Filbur’s length or area differs from Unicel’s, the cartridge page carries the note, the way the Master Spas 6CH-352 page does.

## How to use the numbers you can still read

- Search the string on the cap, whatever prefix it has. C-, FC-, P-, PRB, PCD, PWK, 6540- and a plain OEM code all go through the same box.

- Read all four columns on the page you land on. If one is blank, believe the blank.

- Read the size line and the top and bottom. Equivalence means those match, not merely that two brands sell “a filter for this spa.”

- If two pages share an OEM number and not an area or a plug or a bottom hole, open both. Sundance C-8326 and C-8327, and Jacuzzi C-4326 and C-4950, are the cases in look-alike Sundance and Jacuzzi filters.

- Then use the retailer buttons on that cartridge page if you want to shop. A search for a Unicel number and a search for the OEM number should be the same physical cartridge only when our page says they are equivalents.

The whole table, including a source for every row, is the downloadable dataset. If a number on your cartridge is missing, the correction address is on the corrections policy.

- Filbur Catalog & Reference Guide: https://filbur.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/Filbur-Catalog-Reference-Guide.pdf

## Spas that use more than one filter cartridge at the same time

URL: https://myspafilter.com/guides/spas-that-use-more-than-one-filter/
Last updated: 2026-10-27

When a hot tub holds two or three cartridges at once, when a slim insert sits inside a pleated filter, and when a second cartridge is only a spare on the shelf.

Some housings are built for more than one cartridge. Leisure Time’s listing for Hot Spring OEM 71825 says many of those models take three of the 6" cartridges[38]. Unicel says Master Spas Eco-Pur systems from 2006 on require two C-8341 cartridges, and a separate inner element is used with them[5]. Sundance’s 680 and 780 manuals describe a pleated filter plus a disposable MicroClean insert, on two different replacement clocks[11][12]. A second set you rotate while one soaks is a spare, which Unicel, Pleatco and Jacuzzi recommend, and it is not the same as a housing that holds two[4][1][10].

## Three different meanings of “two filters”

Owners get sold a two-pack and then are not sure whether both cartridges go in the spa today. The documents use “two” in three ways, and only one of them means the housing is full when a single cartridge is installed.

- The housing holds more than one at the same time. You replace every cartridge that was in the well, because each one is part of the flow path.

- One pleated cartridge and one smaller insert occupy the same well and are not the same part. They can have different lifetimes and different cleaning rules.

- A spare set waits while the set in the spa gets dirty. The spare is not installed on top of a full housing.

A retail “2-pack” is usually the third meaning, or simply how the manufacturer boxes the part. Intex 29001E is a two-pack of Type S1 cartridges. Intex’s pages do not say a PureSpa holds an S1 and an S2 together. They say which set numbers take which type. That split is in Intex and Bestway filters.

## Hot Spring wells that hold three

The 6" × 10-1/2" open cartridge C-6430 (OEM 31489 / 71825 / 71826) is the Highlife size. The Leisure Time listing for 71825 says many of these models take three cartridges, and that some models of the same footprint use a Tri-X ceramic filter instead of pleated media. Use the pleated cartridge only where the spa specifies 71825 or a listed equivalent[38].

If you open the well and see three pleated cartridges, order three of the part that matches, not one. If you see a ceramic block, C-6430 is the wrong object even though the footprint is the one the listing mentions. The collection-by-collection sizes, including the 8-1/2" cartridge and the 2018 Limelight cartridge that is not this 6" part, are in Hot Spring filter sizes by collection. Hot Spot models that the dealer assigns to this cartridge are on the Hot Spot page; count the filters in that housing too, because several Hot Spot tubs are listed with more than one.

## Master Spas: two outers, plus an inner

Unicel’s note on C-8341 is direct: from 2006 onward this Eco-Pur outer is a 40 sq ft cartridge and two of them are required. Each one is 8" × 6-3/4" with 4" open ends and a raised ring. The 2002–2005 outer is the different part C-7330, 7" × 7-1/4", 30 sq ft. The inner element C-3310AM is 3-7/8" × 7" and is used with either outer. Unicel calls that inner piece antimicrobial media[5].

Buying one C-8341 leaves the housing half serviced if both outers were due. Buying a C-8341 for a 2004 spa ignores the 7" versus 8" change. The stand-pipe note on the threaded Master Spas replacements is a separate installation step and is explained in Master Spas Eco-Pur filters.

## Sundance’s outer cartridge and disposable insert

Sundance’s 2024 manuals describe a two-stage arrangement rather than two copies of one cartridge. On the 680 Series, the pleated MicroClean Mini filter is on a 12-month replacement and the insert is on a 4-month replacement. On the 780 Series, the small disposable MicroClean cartridge is replaced every 3 months, or earlier[11][12]. Those are not suggestions from a retailer. They are the intervals in the owner’s manuals.

The cleaning rules differ inside the same well. Sundance says not to use filter cleaners on the inner inserts. The 680 manual calls for a high-pressure hose nozzle on the outer pleated filter and a low-pressure nozzle with no chemicals on the insert[11]. Unicel’s one-hour degreaser soak is written for a pleated cartridge you intend to reuse[4]. It is the wrong soak for the insert Sundance says not to chemically clean. Replace the insert on its short interval. Clean or replace the outer on its longer one. Our general cleaning steps are in how to clean a hot tub filter, with that Sundance exception spelled out.

## A cage is not a second cartridge

Bullfrog’s coreless filters are a pleated element plus a plastic cage and cap. Leisure Time says the cage and cap must be installed with OEM 10-00281 and 10-00282, and it names a cage assembly for specific years[43][42]. You do not stack two coreless socks to make up for a missing cage. You install the cage the listing calls for, or you confirm the spa has moved to the Simplicity flat filter that the 10-00282 listing assigns to 2023-and-newer A Series models. The thread-versus-coreless split is in Bullfrog threaded and coreless filters.

## The spare set, which is the recommendation you can apply to any of these

Unicel and Pleatco tell owners to keep two sets and alternate them. The set that comes out gets a hose rinse and a degreasing soak of at least an hour, overnight if you can, and then it dries. The other set goes into the spa so you are not running without filtration[4][1]. Jacuzzi gives the same advice and adds that a cartridge may be reinstalled damp, while a full dry extends its life[10]. For a three-cartridge Hot Spring well, a “set” is three cartridges, not one. For a two-cartridge Eco-Pur well, a set is two outers, and the inner element is its own part. For a Sundance two-stage well, the spare you rotate is the pleated outer; the insert is a disposable on a shorter clock, not a piece you soak and put back.

Running while a set soaks, with nothing in the well, is the case Jacuzzi and Hot Spring reject[10][9]. The consequences — weak jets, high-limit trips, flow codes — are in what a clogged or missing filter does. Putting the spare in without overtightening the retainer is in how to install a hot tub filter.

## How to count yours

- Power off, then remove every cartridge and lay them in a row[9][10].

- If they are the same part, count them. That count is what you replace.

- If one is much smaller, or is a thin insert inside a pleated cartridge, treat it as a different part number and a different interval.

- Read the OEM number off one of the large cartridges and search it here. The page’s fitment notes are where “three required” or “two required” is written when a source says it.

- Order that many, and order a second set only if you want the rotation. Do not install the spare set in a housing that is already full.

## Model-year fitment

## Which filter does my Hot Spring hot tub take? Lookup by model and year

URL: https://myspafilter.com/fitment/hot-spring-filter-by-model-year/

Find the Hot Spring filter part number (71825, 71827, 79435 Tri-X, 78161 and more) for your Highlife, Limelight, Hot Spot, Tiger River or Solana model and year.

The dealer fitment table lists six Hot Spring factory cartridge numbers across these collections: 71825 (pleated, 6" × 10-1/2"), 71827 (8-1/2" × 10-1/2", 65 sq ft), 79435 (Tri-X), 78161 (Limelight 2018 and newer), 78286 (Limelight Prism) and 77004 (Limelight Gleam). The same model name can change cartridge by year, for example Limelight Flair and Pulse take the 71827 for 2008–2017 and the 78161 for 2018–2026. Find your model below, then confirm against the part number on your old cartridge.

## Highlife: pleated cartridge or Tri-X?

For many Highlife models the dealer table lists both the pleated 71825 and the Tri-X 79435 over the same years. The dealer’s note says to use the pleated cartridge only where the spa specifies 71825 or its listed equivalent, and that models requiring Tri-X must use a Tri-X filter. Hot Spring’s own filter article says its Tri-X is compatible with all Highlife Collection models, including those that did not come with one as standard, and gives replacement intervals of 2–3 years for polyester cartridges and 4–6 years for Tri-X. If your spa came with Tri-X cartridges, stay with Tri-X.

## Where the dealer tables differ

Model-year ranges are not identical between dealers. For the Aria, this page’s main source lists Aria AR for 2007–2018, while another Hot Spring dealer’s Tri-X listing gives Aria 2007–2015. Ranges for a model’s first and last year are the least reliable part of any dealer table.

## How to confirm yours

- Read the part number on the old cartridge, or on the filter label if it has worn off.
- If you cannot read it, measure the diameter and length: a 6" × 10-1/2" cartridge is the 71825 family and an 8-1/2" × 10-1/2" one is the 71827 family. Our filter-size guide shows how.
- Check how many cartridges your spa takes in your owner’s manual; we do not list counts per model.

## Which filter does my Caldera hot tub take? Lookup by model and year

URL: https://myspafilter.com/fitment/caldera-filter-by-model-year/

Find the Caldera filter part number (73531, 73532, 73722, 74817, 74148, 76136) for your Utopia, Paradise, Highland or Vacanza model and year, with Unicel equivalents.

The dealer fitment table lists seven Caldera cartridge numbers across these series, and several models switch cartridge partway through their run: for example the Utopia Geneva, Niagara and Tahitian take the 7" × 14-3/4" 73531 through 2004 and the 8" × 16-1/2" 73722 from 2005. Most current Paradise models (Salina, Reunion, Seychelles, Makena) are listed for 73531, and Kauai and Martinique for the shorter 73532. Find your model below and confirm against the number on the old cartridge, because the dealer table flags several model-years as needing a serial-number check.

## Where the dealer tables differ

The model-year table here comes from a single dealer, and other listings do not match it exactly. That dealer’s own product page for the 73531 gives Tahitian as 2002–2005 and Elation as 2003–2008, while its fitment guide gives Paradise Tahitian TAA as 2000–2005 and Elation as 2003–2004 for the 73531 (it moves Elation 2005–2008 to the 73722). A second retailer lists the 73531 for the Paradise series as 2003 to current, and sells the 8" × 16-1/2", 100 sq ft cartridge for the Utopia Geneva from 2005 on, which agrees with the table below. Treat first and last years as approximate.

## How to confirm yours

- Read the part number printed on the old cartridge. The dealer itself says that even within one Caldera model line the filter can change by year, and that the part number is the most reliable method.
- Measure the diameter and length if it is unreadable: 7" × 14-3/4" is the 73531 family, 7" × 10-3/4" the 73532, and 8" × 16-1/2" the 73722 or 74817. Our filter-size guide shows how.
- For the model-years flagged above, have the spa serial number ready and ask a Caldera dealer.

## Which filter does my Jacuzzi hot tub take? Lookup by collection, model and year

URL: https://myspafilter.com/fitment/jacuzzi-filter-by-model-year/
Last updated: 2026-10-26

Jacuzzi filter part numbers (373045, 2540-381, 6000-383A, 6473-157/161 and more) for J-100, J-200, J-300, J-400, J-500 and J-LX models by year, from two published tables, with Unicel, Pleatco and Filbur equivalents.

It depends on the collection and, for several models, the year. In the two published tables we compared, most J-200 and J-100 models take the 373045 (4-15/16" × 13-5/16"), while the J-230 from 2008, J-270 and J-280 take the 2540-381 (8" × 15-1/2"). J-300 spas take two 6000-383A ProClear 60 sq ft cartridges. Current J-400, J-500 and J-LX spas use a three-filter set: a 6473-157 pleated upper, a 6473-161 micron lower and a 6000-383A for the jet pump. Older J-400s (2006–2012) used different parts, and the 2023+ J-200 ProClassic uses an oval 6541-853.

## Find your model

Rows combine two dealer tables: Spa World’s Jacuzzi filter guide (Australia) and the March 2024 Jacuzzi Direct filter table published by a French Jacuzzi dealer. Where they give different years, both are shown. Skimmer and filter bags (6570-392, 6570-398, 2540-389) and the J-LX weir (6540-188) are listed in those tables too but are not cartridges, so they are left out here.

## Where the two tables differ

- J-235 before 2012: only the French table covers it, and it lists the 35 sq ft 6000-136. Spa World starts the J-235 at 2012 with the 373045.

- J-270 and J-280 start year: 2005 in the French table, 2007 in Spa World’s.

- J-LX / J-LXL end year for the two-ProClear setup: 2021 (Spa World) vs 2022 (France). Both move to the 157/161/383 set for 2023.

- J-465 cut-over: France says before May 2007 for 2000-498 and May 2007–2011 for 2540-383; Spa World words it as “up to April 2007” and “up to May 2011”. A 2007 J-465 needs a look at the old cartridge.

- J-400 end year: Spa World lists 2013–2023 for the named J-400 models; the French table says 2013 onward with no end.

Both tables come from dealers outside the US (Australia and France), and we found no public fitment table from Jacuzzi itself, so treat the years as a strong guide rather than a guarantee.

## How to confirm yours

- Read the part number printed on the old cartridge. Expect a J suffix on some (373045J, 6473-157J).
- Jacuzzi’s owners center says filters are sold through local dealers, and that the spa serial number is in the equipment bay on top of the load box, typically 9 digits starting with 100. Give a dealer the serial if the year is near a change-over.
- If the label is gone, measure diameter and length (our filter-size guide shows how) and compare with the sizes above. A J-400 or J-500 with a short upper cartridge and a small closed-end lower one is the 157/161 set.

## Which filter does my Sundance hot tub take? Lookup by model, year and serial number

URL: https://myspafilter.com/fitment/sundance-filter-by-model-year/

Sundance filter part numbers for every model from 1995 to 2024+ (MicroClean, MicroClean Ultra, Ultra II, MicroClean Mini, 373045 and older cartridges), with serial ranges and Unicel, Pleatco and Filbur equivalents.

Sundance changed filter systems several times, so the year matters. In Sundance Spas Norway’s model table: 880 and 980 Series spas from about 2005/2006 to 2023 take the two-piece MicroClean Ultra set (6473-165 outer + 6473-164 inner), with the one-piece 6540-488 as an alternative; 780 Series spas take the two-part MicroClean (6540-501 pleated + 6540-502 disposable upper), also with 6540-488 as the alternative; 680 Series spas through 2022 take the 373045 and 2023+ models take the MicroClean Mini (6473-249S + 6473-283S); and 2024+ 880 models take MicroClean Ultra II (6473-452S + 6473-453S). Pre-2002 spas mostly use the 6540-490 or 6540-483.

Berkely, Brook and Paisley (2020 on, serials starting E2…) are listed with SC817. We could not find that number in any of the three aftermarket catalogs, so confirm it with a Sundance dealer.

## Which system is in my spa, and how often does it need attention?

A Sundance dealer, The Sundance Spa Store, publishes these care intervals by system:

Series and systemCleanReplace
680 Series 2006–2022 (373045 style)MonthlyEvery 12 months
680 Series 2023+ (MicroClean Mini)Outer every 2–3 monthsOuter every 12–18 months; Mini inner every 3–4 months
780 Series (two-piece MicroClean)—Pleated outer every 12–18 months; MicroClean upper every 3–5 months
880 / 980 Series (MicroClean Ultra)—Inner core every 6–9 months

Filbur prints “Replace after 3 months of use” on its FC-2812 version of the 6540-502 disposable upper. For our general advice, see how often to replace a hot tub filter.

## Where the sources differ

- 880 Series, 2005–2008. Leisure Time Inc. lists the 6540-507 MicroClean Plus for 880 Maxxus, Cameo and Optima 2005–2008 and Altamar, Majesta, Marin and Capri 2006–2008. Sundance Norway puts those models on the MicroClean Ultra 6473-165/164 from 2005 or 2006. Check the old cartridge: the MicroClean Plus is a single cartridge, the Ultra is an outer plus an inner core.

- 980 Series start and end dates. Leisure Time lists Claremont and Kingston for 2017–2025. A Sundance dealer (Snow Valley Spas) lists Claremont and Kingston from October 2016, and Lisbon and Odessa for 2019–March 2021. Sundance Norway gives 2017+ and 2019+.

- Bahia, Cayman, Palermo and Lagunas 2003–2005, Capri 2001 and Caprio 2000–2001. Sundance Norway lists the one-piece 6540-488 as the main filter for these and the 501/502 pair as the alternative, the reverse of later 780 models.

- 680 Series, early 2023. Leisure Time says some early-2023 680 spas may still use the 373045. The serial ranges above are the best way to tell.

- 2024 and 2026 changes. Leisure Time says to confirm the system on 2024 880 spas, and lists a MicroClean Ultra II Lite for 2026 780 models (Bristol, Chelsee, Dover, Hamilton, Montclair) using a 6473-608S outer with the 6473-453S inner. Sundance Norway’s table does not list the Ultra II Lite yet.

- Pre-2006 vs 2006+ one-piece cartridges. Unicel splits the 6540-488 into C-8326 (with core plug, for pre-2006 spas) and C-8327 (no plug, after 2005). Leisure Time’s tables follow the same split.

Sundance Norway is a European distributor, and Leisure Time and Snow Valley are North American dealers. Model names match across them, but production dates can differ by market.

## How to confirm yours

- Read the part number on the old cartridge or cartridges. A two-piece set (outer plus inner core) is MicroClean Ultra or Mini; a pleated cartridge plus a short disposable top is MicroClean.
- Compare your spa’s serial number with the ranges in the table above, as Sundance Norway advises.
- If the label is unreadable, measure diameter and length (see our filter-size guide) and compare with the sizes above.

## Which filter does my Bullfrog hot tub take? Lookup by series and year

URL: https://myspafilter.com/fitment/bullfrog-filter-by-model-year/
Last updated: 2026-10-27

Bullfrog Spas filter part numbers by series and model year, 1997 to 2026: 10-1086, 10-1085, 10-2785, 10-2870, coreless 10-00282 and 10-00281, Simplicity flat filters and CALM, with Unicel, Pleatco and Filbur equivalents and sizes.

It depends on the series and the year. Per Bullfrog’s own parts store: A Series 2018–2022, R Series and X Series from 2018 take the coreless 10-00282 (2-pack 10-00416); STIL from 2018 takes the smaller coreless 10-00281 (2-pack 10-00810); A Series from 2023, M Series and Swim Series use Simplicity flat filters 10-00814. Older spas take threaded cartridges: 10-2870 for A/R/X 2013–2016, 10-2785 for 2003–2012, 10-1085 for 2000–2002 and 10-1086 for 1997–1999. A 2013–2017 A/R/X or 2015–2017 STIL can switch to coreless filters by fitting the 10-00417 cage and cap assembly.

## Find your series and year

Bullfrog sorts its filters by series and build year rather than by individual model, so the table works the same way: an A7L, A8 or any other A Series spa uses the A Series row for its year. Years come from the product pages on Bullfrog’s own parts store, cross-checked against Leisure Time Inc.’s fitment guide and the list kept by Bullfrog Spa Parts Charlottesville, a Bullfrog dealer.

## Threaded or coreless: how to tell in ten seconds

Lift out the cartridge. If a plastic cage stays in the spa and the pleated sleeve slides off it, you have the coreless system (10-00282 or 10-00281). If the whole cartridge unscrews as one piece with a handle on top, it is a threaded cartridge (10-2870 or older). For A (2022 and earlier), R, X and STIL spas, Bullfrog’s filter-care article describes removal as turning the filter-core cap counter-clockwise and sliding the cartridge up off the core. A flat, rectangular filter is a Simplicity filter.

## Where the sources disagree

- When coreless started. Bullfrog’s store and Leisure Time say 2018. Pleatco labels both coreless cross-references (PBF40, PBF17) “2017–Current”, and labels the threaded PBF36 “2013–2017”. Bullfrog’s store limits the original 10-2870 to 2013–2016, while its cage-assembly page offers the conversion for 2013–2017 spas. For a 2017 spa, look at what is installed.

- R Series end year. Bullfrog’s 10-00416 page says R Series 2018 and later; Leisure Time and Southern Leisure Spas say R Series 2018–2022.

- Coreless in pre-2013 spas. The Charlottesville dealer lists 10-00282 for “All 2003–2012 except STIL” when used with the 10-00417 cage, and Hot Tub Outpost says 2002 and newer except STIL. Bullfrog’s own cage page only claims 2013 and newer. If your spa is older than 2013, ask a dealer before buying the cage.

- Size and rating of the coreless filters. 10-00282: 7-3/4" × 5-3/4" and 50 sq ft (Leisure Time) vs 8" × 6-1/4" (Pleatco, Southern Leisure, Hot Tub Outpost) and 30 sq ft for Pleatco’s PBF40. 10-00281: about 27 sq ft (Leisure Time) vs 18 sq ft (Pleatco PBF17).

- Rating of the threaded cartridges. The Charlottesville dealer and Filbur call 10-1035 a 35 sq ft cartridge, and Unicel notes the original is 35 sq ft, but Unicel rates its own 8CH-950 at 50. Unicel’s 8CH-951 (for 10-2870) appears as 50 sq ft in the Bullfrog listing and 40 in the spec table.

- Is 10-2870 for 2003 on? The Charlottesville dealer describes 10-2870 as “2003–Present except STIL” because it replaces 10-2785; Bullfrog’s store describes it as the original cartridge for 2013–2016 A/R/X spas.

## Known limits

- No source we found gives dimensions for 10-1085, 10-1086, 10-3430, the Simplicity filters or the CALM filter, and none of the three aftermarket catalogs lists them.

- No catalog lists an aftermarket version of the Simplicity or CALM filters.

- The 10-1035 is listed by Unicel and Filbur, but no source we found says which years it was fitted.

## How to confirm yours

- Read the number on the old cartridge’s end cap or label and search it here.
- No number? Measure diameter and length (our filter-size guide shows how). A threaded 8" × about 6" cartridge is the 10-2870/10-2785 family; a coreless 8" sleeve is 10-00282; a coreless sleeve under 7" is the STIL 10-00281.
- Bullfrog’s care article says to clean pleated cartridges every 3–6 weeks and replace them every 1–2 years; see also how often to clean a hot tub filter.

Older Legacy and FreedomYears not givenX268080 (some use X268300 or X268526)
Contractor SeriesUp to 2011 / 2012X268519 (now X268558) / X268554; CS 415: X268521
Instinct2025 / 2026X268554 / X268563

## Where the sources disagree

- 2025–2026 Clarity. The Suntek chart lists X268568. Suntek’s own X268566 listing says Clarity spas made on or after 15 April 2026 take X268566 and earlier 2025 models X268568. Masterspaparts.com says Master Spas changed the Clarity filter during 2026 and associates X268569 with “updated Clarity and Getaway” lines. Check the cartridge before ordering.

- 2025 H2X swim spas. Suntek lists X268566 + X268532 + X268560 for most 2025 H2X models (and notes that the factory store lists X268559 for “most 2025 H2X”). Masterspaparts.com gives X268559 for most H2X swim spas.

- X268572. Suntek treats it as a late-production stamping of X268560. Masterspaparts.com presents it as the cartridge for most 2025 Twilight, MP Legend, Living Healthy and many H2X models.

- X268568. Masterspaparts.com says it is exclusively for the TS 240; Suntek also lists it for 2025 Clarity.

- Old-style Eco-Pur years. Pleatco labels PMA10 (X268057) “Eco-pur replacement 2004 and later”; Suntek puts X268057 in 2001–2003 spas and the black-standpipe X268546 set from 2004. Unicel splits its Eco-Pur outer cartridges as C-7330 for 2002–2005 and C-8341 (two required) for 2006 on.

- X268546 size. Unicel’s 6CH-352 is 6" × 8"; Suntek lists the factory part at 6.5" × 7.75". Unicel says to remove the black standpipe when using 6CH-352.

- Healthy Living years. Suntek lists 2013–2016 and 2017–2021, and notes the factory tables show 2018–2020.

## Known limits

- None of the three aftermarket catalogs lists X268548, X268549, X268550 or any 2025-platform part by number, and Suntek says there is no aftermarket EcoPur Charge.

- Suntek marks several lines as “confirm with serial”: Clarity CLS 360/415 (2013–2015), Getaway Caribbean (2014–2016), Living Healthy L5–S7 (2025 on) and Michael Phelps Xtreme. We do not list a filter for them. For the LH line, Suntek reports that Master Spas’ official part finder shows a single cartridge, X268543 for 2023–2024 LH6/LH7 and X268560 for 2025–2026 LH6/LH7.

- Sizes for X268546 to X268569 come from one dealer’s listings; Master Spas publishes no public spec sheet that we found.

## How to confirm yours

- Read the X2685xx number on the old cartridge and search it here.
- Use the serial number. Per Suntek, on most spas built since 2009 the first two digits are the model year (22… = 2022); Getaway serials start with R, swim spas with H, and spas built before 2009 start with M.
- 2025 cartridges do not fit older housings. Suntek says adapters X251168 and X251169 exist to retrofit 2025 filters into earlier spas.
- Citing Master Spas’ owner’s manuals, Suntek suggests rinsing the pleated cartridges weekly, soaking them monthly, replacing them about every 12 months, and replacing the EcoPur Charge every 6 months. See also how often to clean a hot tub filter.
